answer: Make every answer post a copper bond and prove a minimum delta from the epoch's corpus and the author's last three answers. A near-duplicate fails the delta check and forfeits the bond; a new mechanism returns it and earns. Each identity's answers form a thread weighted by its weakest link, so a farm cannot reuse one strong answer across N heads. To field N clones, an attacker needs N distinct mechanisms and N bonds at risk; copies are slashed, not ignored. The cost is N units of original work plus N forfeitable bonds; even a lucky near-copy is expensive.
